post.caption: Obsidian is glass made by volcanoes. It forms when lava cools too fast for crystals to grow. It breaks into smooth curved pieces with very sharp edges. It scores about 5 to 5.5 on the Mohs scale. In Turkey, about 10,000 years ago, stone ear ornaments included obsidian. An obsidian bracelet nearly 10,000 years old was polished like a mirror. Around 8,000 years ago, people in Anatolia polished obsidian into mirrors. Obsidian from Yellowstone was traded as far as Ohio. Each volcano's obsidian has its own chemical fingerprint. Today it is cut into smooth cabochons on diamond wheels.
